title: Implement prefetch safety gates and eviction-priority rewrite to prevent cross-tenant cache poisoning
creator: Samir Patel
description:
Summary: A recent capacity/regression incident revealed a subtle cross-tenant poisoning vector in the KV/prefix cache introduced by the aggressive prefetch path. Prefetch writes were promoted to live entries before validation under certain eviction pressure scenarios, and the eviction scoring logic allowed low-confidence prefetched items to displace verified entries. This created stale/mismatched entries served to downstream requests, causing correctness regressions and customer-facing anomalies in a small but high-impact set of requests.

Goal: Implement a multi-layer mitigation: quarantine prefetch entries until validated, make eviction scoring tenant-aware and deterministic, add admission controls under memory pressure, and strengthen tests and telemetry to prevent regressions.
impact_summary: Customer-visible incorrect responses observed for ~12 customer sessions during the incident window, with elevated error rates for small-context workloads. Latency improved briefly after the prefetch experiment but correctness regressions made the change unacceptable. Affected customers were on Dedicated capacity clusters that experienced high eviction churn. Estimated root-cause blast radius: ~1% of requests on impacted clusters during peak traffic windows.
root_cause: Prefetch path wrote provisional entries directly into the live prefix cache and relied on an eviction priority that favored recency over origin-trust. Under high allocation churn the provisional entries bypassed validation and displaced canonical entries because eviction score didn't incorporate origin confidence or tenant isolation. Additionally, the cache key namespace allowed subtle collisions when canonicalization logic and prefetch key generation diverged for edge tokenization cases.
resolution: Short-term mitigation: rolled back the prefetch write path to write-only provisional cache (in-memory transient) and reverted eviction priority changes in runtime-1.19. Medium-term fix: implement quarantine layer, tenant-scoped key hashing, and deterministic eviction scoring that includes origin confidence and per-tenant weight. Instrumentation and tests added to detect any future cross-tenant displacement. Patch landed and is under canary in runtime-1.20 branch.
actions: AX1: Implement 'quarantine' cache state for prefetched entries (owner: Lin Zhao, due: 2026-03-22) - prefetched entries must not be served until validated by an LRU confirmation or explicit write-through event.
AX2: Change eviction scoring to include fields: origin_confidence_score, tenant_weight, insertion_phase (provisional vs verified). (owner: Marco Ruiz, due: 2026-03-25)
AX3: Enforce tenant-scoped key canonicalization to avoid namespace collisions (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2026-03-20)
AX4: Add admission control circuit for prefetch under high memory pressure (owner: Lin Zhao, due: 2026-03-27) - drop or delay prefetch when eviction rate > threshold.
AX5: Add deterministic unit+integration test harness for eviction races and a fuzz suite for key canonicalization mismatches (owner: Marco Ruiz, due: 2026-03-31)
AX6: Create a runbook for triaging prefetched-entry anomalies with suggested Grafana queries and alert thresholds (owner: Samir Patel, due: 2026-03-18)
AX7: Instrument per-tenant eviction telemetry and add a dashboard and SLO gate for eviction-induced correctness regressions (owner: Data Eng Team, due: 2026-03-29)
AX8: Security review and threat modeling for cross-tenant contamination scenarios (owner: Emma Fischer, due: 2026-03-24)
AX9: Rollout plan: canary on 5% of Dedicated clusters with runtime-1.20, monitor eviction-score distributions and correctness, then 25%/75% rollouts. (owner: Lin Zhao, due: 2026-04-01)
AX10: Customer communication: prepare targeted notes for affected customers and CS handoff materials (owner: Customer Ops, due: 2026-03-19)
updates: 2026-03-05: Ticket opened after post-incident debrief; preliminary rollback executed to stop prefetch writes to live cache. Action list drafted.
2026-03-07: Engineering sync: agreed to quarantine approach over full rollback to preserve latency benefits; trade-off: slight increase in cold-miss rate for prefetched keys during validation window.
2026-03-09: Design review with infra and security; flagged tenant key canonicalization as mandatory. Security requested threat model for intentional poisoning.
2026-03-11: PR #8421 created: preliminary eviction-score refactor. Internal review suggested to add origin_confidence field and avoid float instability in scoring algorithm.

2026-03-13: Canary patch queued for runtime-1.20 canary next deploy; added additional unit tests to simulate eviction storms. QA found a deterministic race in reference counter path; added AX5 to address.
2026-03-14: Observability team added per-tenant eviction metrics to internal dashboard; initial baseline captured for affected clusters. Security review kickoff scheduled.
Note: updated_at reflects latest activity where telemetry baseline was established.
risk_assessment: Medium-high: changes touch core eviction path and key canonicalization. The quarantine approach limits blast radius but adds potential latency regressions for prefetch benefits. Thorough canarying and telemetry required before wide rollout.
testing_plan: Unit tests for eviction scoring determinism, integration tests simulating heavy churn across multiple tenants, fuzzing for canonicalization divergence, and e2e correctness checks under a canary fleet. Add CI gate that runs eviction-fuzz smoke on nightly builds.
code_review_notes: Prefer integer scoring buckets to avoid float nondeterminism across platforms. Reviewers requested explicit comments documenting tenant-weight calculation and fallback behavior when tenant_weight config missing. Keep changes small and reversible for canary.
notes_for_release: runtime-1.20 includes quarantine layer, eviction-score rewrite, tenant-key-canonicalization, and additional telemetry. Release notes must include rollback instructions and circuit breaker thresholds for prefetch admission.
